prompt: In a trial of a new headache pill, half the subjects receive the pill and half receive an identical-looking sugar pill, and no subject knows which they got. What is the main purpose of the sugar pill?

choices.label: So that both groups experience the same expectation of relief, letting the pill's real effect be separated from the placebo effect
To make the experiment take less time

hint: People often feel better just because they believe they were treated. That is the placebo effect.

hints.text: People often feel better just because they believe they were treated. That is the placebo effect.
If only one group took a pill, feeling better could come from belief alone. Give everyone a pill so belief is equal in both groups.
The sugar pill equalizes expectations so any difference is due to the medicine: choice B.

explanation: Subjects who think they are being treated often report improvement even from a fake treatment: the placebo effect.
By giving the control group an identical placebo, both groups get the same expectation. Any extra improvement in the pill group must come from the pill itself.
This is a control with blinding. Choice B.

alternativeExplanations.title: Blinding, too
steps: Because the pills look identical and subjects do not know their group, the study is blind.
If the doctors evaluating headaches also do not know, it is double-blind, removing their expectations as well.
Placebo plus blinding is standard in good medical experiments.
